OUR ETHOS
Our ethos is to create a federation of schools where children succeed and are proud of their achievements. We strive to actively promote British values and prepare our children to become role models, thus preparing them for life in modern Britain. To do this, we create a respectful, inclusive atmosphere that is welcoming, fun, friendly and safe. We are a federation that nurtures curiosity and creativity through an inspiring, challenging and engaging curriculum, where learning is at the heart of all that we do. Our children learn to become resilient and self-assured in an environment where success is celebrated.Our ethos is delivered through these aims for our children:
Through the aims of the Federation, we actively promote lifelong learning whilst ensuring the children respect one another, enjoy their school experiences and achieve their personal best.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher | NEWTONS PRIMARY SCHOOL
pageCache.text:
NEWTONS PRIMARY SCHOOL
WELCOME TO OUR SCHOOL!
At Newtons Primary School, we pride ourselves on fostering a nurturing and inclusive environment where every child is encouraged to achieve their full potential. Our dedicated staff work tirelessly to ensure that each student feels valued, supported and inspired to succeed, both academically and personally. We are committed to delivering high-quality education and we strive to create a vibrant learning experience that cultivates curiosity, creativity and critical thinking.
As you and your child settle into school life, we understand that joining a new school can feel like a big step, both for students and families. Please know that we are here to support you every step of the way. If you have any questions or concerns, our teachers, administrative staff and senior leaders are always available to assist you. We also encourage you to participate in school activities and events, as this is a wonderful way to become involved in the community and to get to know other families.
Our school values the strong partnership between home and school and we believe that working together is key to ensuring your child’s success. Communication will be an important part of this collaboration and we will keep you informed of key dates, important announcements and your child’s progress throughout the year.
Once again, thank you for choosing Newtons Primary School and we look forward to watching your child achieve their personal best!
Alicia Argire - Headteacher

NEWTONS PRIMARY SCHOOL
Collective Worship at Newtons Primary School
By Law, all maintained schools must provide religious education and daily collective worship for all students.
Collective Worship aims to promote spiritual, moral and cultural development.
It is compulsory for all schools to perform an act of collective worship daily unless students ask for an exemption. At Newtons it takes place in our daily school assemblies and classes.
Newtons encourage children to reflect upon their own beliefs while taking part and this is built on our values of GREAT.

NEWTONS PRIMARY SCHOOL
CORNERSTONES AT NEWTONS
Our school is an exciting place to learn. Our vision is to inspire every child to be a lifelong learner, who is empowered to succeed and achieve their full potential.
The aim of our curriculum is to provide a broad and balanced subject range which challenges, engages and children enjoy learning.
Cornerstones CurriculumThis is an exciting topic based curriculum, with pupil engagement and creativity at its heart. Each unit lasts for a complete half term and across the course of time all aspects of the National Curriculum are covered.
This programme embraces most curriculum subjects giving pupils a rounded learning experience where all of the subjects of the curriculum are interlinked.
MathematicsIn addition to the Cornerstones curriculum, we also have our White Rose Maths curriculum. This supports our discrete teaching of maths and ensures the children are able to access different levels of challenge and depth of application. We also give children the opportunity to learn and practice mental maths skills daily in a short ten for 10 session. We promote the use and understanding of maths throughout our curriculum, encouraging children to use and apply their skills in science, geography, history, design technology and art.
EnglishWe use a book based approach which entails using quality key texts to help develop the skills of spoken language, reading and writing in accordance with the National Curriculum. Children get exciting opportunities to write for a range of purposes, applying their grammatical handwriting and spelling skills.
Our prime approach to early reading is synthetic phonics. This builds the children's understanding of how words are constructed. Children learn how to put sounds together to make complete words and then how to break words apart to spell them. We teach children to develop comprehension skills to ensure that they understand what they read and develop skills of inference, deduction and factual retrieval. Through reading a range of text types, the children are taught comprehension skills such as summarising, predicting, inferring and retrieving. We are keen to develop children's vocabulary and consequently the use of thesauruses and dictionaries is encouraged. The children have access to a wide range of texts which they are able to take home and share with their families.
Handwriting and SpellingWe have high expectations of our pupils' spelling and presentation. We insist on accurate letter formation using the Nelsons handwriting scheme. By Upper Key Stage 2 children are encouraged to use pen for the majority of their writing, using a practical, fluid handwriting style. From Year 1 to Year 6 we use the Newtons Spelling programme for accuracy in spelling the 1000 high frequency words.
PEOur PE lessons are taught using the Val Sabin PE scheme and LCP which leads our children through the many aspects of PE including gymnastics, athletics and developing a wide variety of skills.
RESchools have to decide the scheme and syllabus they use for teaching RE. In this school we use the Havering RE Syllabus.

P.E
ReceptionYear 1Year 2Year 5Year 6
At Newtons, we are committed to providing a Physical Education curriculum that is inclusive, engaging and inspiring for all pupils. From Nursery onwards, every child participates in PE lessons designed to develop fundamental movement skills, teamwork and a lifelong appreciation of physical activity.
All pupils are given the opportunity to take part in a wide variety of sports. They practise and refine their skills both individually and in group situations, with a strong emphasis on co-operation, respect and consideration for others. As they progress through the school, pupils build on these foundations and participate in high-quality sporting experiences that challenge and motivate them to achieve their best.
The government’s continued investment in the Primary PE and Sport Premium enables us to broaden the range of opportunities available to our children. We firmly believe that exposing pupils to as many different sporting experiences as possible empowers them to discover activities they enjoy, develop confidence, and identify any natural talents they may wish to pursue further.
We also benefit from a strong partnership with our local sports collective and neighbouring schools. This collaboration allows us to participate in local events and competitions, promoting both physical education and healthy lifestyles within our wider community. In addition, we are fortunate to have a specialist PE teacher whose expertise ensures that all children receive high-quality instruction and enjoy positive, meaningful experiences in sport and physical activity.
Sports taught at Newtons
At Newtons, we proudly host two much-anticipated annual events: Sports Day and our Big Dance Afternoon.
Our aim is for every child to take part, enjoy the experience, and strive to achieve their personal best. These events are not only about friendly competition and performance, but also about teamwork, confidence, resilience and, most importantly, fun.
We celebrate all of our children’s efforts and achievements during our assemblies, recognising participation, determination and success at every level.
Learning to swim is an essential life skill and an important part of the primary school curriculum. We organise swimming lessons for all children in Year 5. This year, Year 6 pupils will also take part, as they previously missed the opportunity.
Lessons take place during the school day and form part of the National Curriculum for Physical Education. Our aim is for every child to be able to swim at least 25 metres confidently by the age of eleven, as well as develop water safety awareness and basic rescue skills.
At Newtons Primary School, we believe it is very important to provide children with opportunities to take part in extracurricular activities. We aim to offer a broad and varied range of clubs so that children of all ages can access and enjoy them.
Our current clubs include a wide selection of sports, giving children the chance to experience different types of physical activity and develop new skills. In addition to sport, we offer creative and well-being clubs that support children’s artistic development and personal growth.
We also extend opportunities for children to engage in extracurricular music through activities such as choir, encouraging creativity, confidence, and a love of performance.

NEWTONS PRIMARY SCHOOL
SPORTS PREMIUM FUNDING
The PE and Sports Grant received has enabled us to enhance the way PE is taught at our school, teaching children the importance of healthy living and how to adopt healthy attitudes to eating and exercise.
At our school, we have chosen to spend our allocation of these funds on providing Sports Coaching for each class, providing resources and training courses in PE, purchasing sports equipment, joining the Havering sports collective, training and support in order to develop collaborative skills, resulting in our pupils experiencing an extended range of sports and games and a variety of sports clubs.
Our pupils have a wider range of opportunity to represent our school in various tournaments and competitions in a wider range of sports.

NEWTONS PRIMARY SCHOOL
ADMISSIONS
Havering Council (the Local Authority) is the admission authority for all community schools in the London Borough of Havering. This means that it is the Council’s responsibility to set the admissions criteria and make the decisions as to which pupils are admitted to this school.
The admission arrangements can be viewed on the following page:
https://www.havering.gov.uk/info/20008/school_admissions/482/school_admissions_arrangements_and_statistics
Applications for children to start Reception in September must be made via your home Local Authority. For parents that live in Havering this website is www.eadmissions.org.uk
IN-YEAR ADMISSIONS
The Havering School Admissions Team manage the In-Year application process on behalf of Newtons Primary School alongside all other schools in Havering. You must therefore apply following the In-Year process set out via www.havering.gov.uk/admissions/inyear.
If your child has not been offered a school place following an in-year application, you have the legal right to appeal this decision to an Independent Appeal Panel.
In Havering, we utilise an external company to facilitate all school appeals.
This company is responsible for clerking, timetabling, and arranging independent panels, ensuring the appeals process is entirely independent of both the school and the Local Authority, providing a fair and impartial review.
In line with the School Admission Appeals Code 2022, all admission appeals will be held online.
This approach has been chosen by the admission authority and appeal panels based on positive feedback from previous online hearings.
For further information regarding the appeals process please click on the link below.
www.havering.gov.uk/admissions/appeal

OUR SCHOOL MILK SCHEME
Did you know our school provides a school milk scheme?
By registering your child for our school milk scheme they will receive a 189ml (third of a pint) carton of semi-skimmed milk every day. This is delivered fresh and chilled to their classroom every day.
“How much does it cost?”
Thanks to government subsidies, school milk is free for all under-fives and is subsided at around £15 a term for children aged five or older.
“Why should I register my child?”
School milk provides your child with essential nutrients. It is also hydrating and energy boosting, helping to bridge the long gap between breakfast and lunch so children stay focused.
